# pixi-effects — full documentation for AI agents

Concatenation of the skill, cheatsheet, pitfalls, recipes and the DSL / API references. Generated by scripts/build-llms.mjs; do not edit.



<!-- ===== skills/pixi-effects/SKILL.md ===== -->

> Written for pixi-effects 0.27.1. Update this skill with `npx skills update`; the newest docs are at https://yjmtmtk.github.io/pixi-effects/

# pixi-effects — write a video as data

You describe a video as a tree of plain objects; the library plays it in a canvas and exports it (MP4/WebM/MOV). You never write per-frame code. **Read `reference/cheatsheet.md` once before writing anything** (about 35 KB: conventions, layer types, keyframes). `reference/recipes.md` (67 KB) is an index of tested recipes: `grep -n "^## " reference/recipes.md`, then read only the one that fits (a title, a lower third, a chart, a kinetic-type line, a 2.5D scene …). `reference/pitfalls.md` (41 KB, numbered) is for when a warning or the picture surprises you: search it for the word, do not read it end to end. A simple title needs the cheatsheet and one recipe, nothing more.

## Workflow

1. **Start from `template.html`** (copy it; it also has the shared loader (`<div class="pe-loader" data-label="LOADING">` + `pixi-effects/loader.css`: HTML and CSS only, animating just `transform` / `opacity`, so it keeps moving while the page builds the video; `movie.init()` fades it out). Keep it; a loader of your own is fine (`pe-loader--custom`) as long as it only animates `transform` / `opacity`, never with JavaScript or `requestAnimationFrame`; it loads the library from a CDN, collects every console warning into `window.__logs`, and exposes `window.movie`). One HTML file, plain JS. Default canvas 1280×720 @ 30 fps.
2. **Give the movie a poster time.** In `movie.init` add `poster: <seconds>`: the most striking moment (a title fully on screen, not the first frame, which is often black). The canvas shows that picture before play (the playhead stays at 0 and play starts from 0), and the check writes it as `poster.jpg`.
3. **Write the composition as data.** Anything repeated (letters, bars, particles, scenes) is a JS function or loop that returns specs — never copy-paste objects. Derive coordinates and times from constants/data, not magic numbers.
4. **Show the human:** `npx pixi-effects view my-video.html` opens their browser on the page with a scrubbable, zoomable timeline under it (click / drag to seek, + / − or Ctrl/⌘ + wheel to zoom); it keeps running until Ctrl-C. **Deliver the file:** `npx pixi-effects render my-video.html -o my-video.mp4` renders the page headless to mp4 / webm / mov / mkv and exits 0 only when the file is written; run it AFTER the check below passes. **Run the check — one command does steps 3, 4 and the export:** `npx pixi-effects check my-video.html` (Node ≥ 22 and Chrome installed). **If `npx` says command not found, or prints nothing** (your npm may hold back a release that is a few days old, or an old release is cached): `npm i pixi-effects`, then `node node_modules/pixi-effects/ai/tools/check.mjs my-video.html` (the same for `render.mjs` and `view.mjs`). It starts its own private Chrome (nothing is shared with other sessions), waits for `window.__ready`, and writes `timeline.html` (every layer as a bar on a time axis: ◆ keyframes, shaded transitions; hand it to the human to open) and prints: console warnings, `movie.inspect` over the WHOLE timeline (grouped), `movie.inspectAudio()`, then exports an mp4 and decodes it again (video size and length, audio length, loudness per second, silence). It writes `check-out/<name>/sheet.png` — **open that picture and look at it** — plus the mp4 and `report.json`. Exit 0 = nothing to fix; exit 1 = a list of problems; fix them and run it again. A key a layer does not have (a typo in a layer key, a keyframe property or a text style key; `anchorX` outside `initial`; `pitch` outside `sfx`) is a warning that names the key and what you probably meant: treat it like any other warning. Text that overlaps text is listed under `review` (not a failure: ghost layers, glow copies and per-letter boxes are often intentional; look at the sheet; `--strict` makes them fail). The manual steps below are for looking at one frame closely. The same judgement is in the page: `await movie.review({ at: 'title@end' })` returns `{ frames, problems, review, fonts, audio, at }` (what `check` prints, as data) and `movie.resolveAt('3.5, title@end')` turns moments into frames.
   **Or by hand: run it and read the logs first.** `window.__ready` must be `true` and `window.__logs` should be `[]`. A pixi-effects warning is an instruction: fix what it names.
5. **Look at it** — you cannot judge motion from code. The library has the tools built in:
   - `await movie.contactSheet({ count: 6, as: 'dataURL' })` → ONE image of several labelled frames (pass `frames: [...]` / `times: [...]` to choose; include the middle of every transition and the last second). Save it and view it.
   - `await movie.inspect(frame)` → every layer's canvas bounds and visibility, plus `issues` (text off the canvas, cut off by an edge, empty, or overlapping other text). Run it at several frames; fix every issue it names.
   - `await movie.snapshot(frame, { as: 'dataURL' })` → one frame, canvas only (no player bar).
   - `movie.inspectAudio()` → **hear with numbers**: for every sound its `start`, `sound.length`, `sound.peakDb`, `sound.loudestAt` (line this up with the picture) and `sound.brightnessHz` (< 500 dark, > 8000 airy), plus `issues` (limited mix, inaudible or cut-off sounds). Check it whenever the movie has audio; `render()` encodes this same mix.
   - **A moment, a movement, the sound (`pixi-effects-check` options):** `--at 3.5,title@end,50%,f120` writes those pictures to `check-out/<name>/frames/*.png` (and `at.png`): the last frame of a layer is `name@end`, the middle `name@mid`. `--onion 1:3` writes `onion.png`, eight frames of seconds 1–3 overlaid (the later the stronger): a trail that shows a movement's path and easing (even steps = constant speed, bunched = slow). `report.audio` now has `loudness` (`integratedLufs`, `truePeakDb`, `clippedSamples`, `silences`), `scenes` (per named top-level composition), `cues` (when each sound starts) and `notes` (advice: quiet or loud for web video, little headroom, silent stretches; web video is typically −14 to −16 LUFS); `waveform.png` draws the mix with the scene edges and the cues. A web font that failed to load fails the check; a text layer none of whose fonts is installed is listed for review.
   - **A deck** (`composition.stops`, `deck()`): `await movie.contactSheet({ frames: movie.stops.map(s => s.frame), as: 'dataURL' })` is one picture of every stop (the check writes it as `stops.png`); what the audience reads while a page waits is that picture, so check every one. `await movie.inspectStops()` lists the stops where the picture is still changing (a stop landing before its animation ends); the check prints it as a review list: move the stop later or flag a settled one `pdf: true`. `await movie.stopImages({ which: 'pages' })` / `movie.exportPDF()` give the pages themselves.
   From a browser tool the result is a `data:` URL string: `agent-browser eval "movie.contactSheet({ count: 6, as: 'dataURL' })" | python3 scripts/save-image.py /absolute/sheet.png`, then open the PNG. Sheet tiles are small (~480 px): use `snapshot` for detail. `inspect` output is long on busy scenes: pass `{ layers: 'none' }` and read `issues` first. Give layers a `name` so inspect paths are readable. A moving ticker is not flagged as cut off.
6. **Iterate** on what you saw (clipped text, collisions, wrong timing). Fast motion looks choppy: add `motionBlur: true` to `movie.init` (render, snapshot and contact sheet then show a film-style blur; renders take ~8× longer). Then export: `const blob = await movie.render({ format: 'mp4' })` (about real time; `movie.on('progress', …)` reports 0–100). **While you iterate, do not export the whole movie:** `check --no-export --at <the moment you changed>` takes seconds (3 to 10 s on the gallery pieces: most of it is loading the page and measuring the sound); to see motion, `render({ range: [from, to] })` / `pixi-effects-render --range 10:15` / `--scene name` exports only that part (picture and sound); `draft: true` / `--draft` is half size, low quality and no motion blur: a much smaller file (a piece that asks for motion blur renders much faster as a draft: 4 s of `hanabi-night` took 14.0 s, and 8.2 s as a draft, about 7 s of either being the browser's start-up), but the drawing itself is not faster. Export the whole movie once, at the end.

## The rules that cause most failures

- **Keyframe `at` starts at 0 when the layer appears** (negative = back from the layer's end). A layer's own `at` and a transition's `at` are composition time.
- **Layers are hidden, not removed, after their lifespan; z-order is array order.** Switch scenes by stacking layers with `at`/`duration` over an opaque background rect.
- **Angles are degrees. `+z` is toward the viewer. Numbers can be expressions** (`'GW/2 - w/2'`; no `pi`; no per-frame variable).
- **Anchors**: rect/circle/ellipse are centred on `x,y`; text and image are top-left (use `anchorX/anchorY: 0.5`); compositions use `pivotX/pivotY`. A bar that grows from its base needs `anchorY: 1`.
- **Sound effects need no files:** `{ type: 'audio', sfx: 'swoosh', at: 2 }` — presets `click pop swoosh swipe hit riser chime beep coin glitch typewriter`; knobs `pitch`, `brightness`, `seed`. The layer lasts as long as the sound (`duration` stretches it); a `riser` is loudest at its end (`at = hit − duration`), a `swoosh` 0.16 s in. A music file shorter than its layer goes silent — `loop: true`.
- **Masks live in the parent's coordinates and don't follow the masked layer.** **`filterArea` is in the layer's own coordinates.** **One mask for several layers: name the layer and write its name as the `mask`** (`mask: 'band'`; `{ layer, channel: 'luma', invert: true }`; a list intersects); the named layer is not drawn and must live as long as its users. A **luma wipe** is a transition: `{ kind: 'luma', map: 'radial' | 'linear' | 'diagonal' | '<grayscale asset>', softness, flip }`.
- **2.5D needs `threeD: true`** on each layer plus a `{ type: 'camera' }` layer; camera props go in `initial`/keyframes; keep every `z` below the camera distance (≈ 989 at 720p, fov 40); under a dolly zoom only `z = 0` stays fixed; **depth of field** is two camera props, `focus` (a threeD layer's name or a z) and `aperture` (30 default, 0 off), and a rack focus is a keyframe on `focus`.
- **Group / parent layers = `{ type: 'null', name: 'rig' }`** (draws nothing, only moves) + `parent: 'rig'` on the layers that should follow it: their `x`/`y` are then measured from the null's origin, and the null's position / rotation / scale / alpha carry them (orbits, clock hands, grouped fades). Nulls chain. Only `null` layers can be parents; not for `threeD` layers.
- **Time:** `speed` (slow motion, backward) and `time` (a curve of the layer's own seconds: freeze, rewind, ramp) on video, audio-file and composition layers; put what you want to rewind in a composition. Children of such a composition are in ITS seconds. `ease: 'cubic-bezier(.4, 0, .2, 1)'` is the CSS curve. See the recipe `rewind-and-replay` and pitfalls 69–73.
- **Built in:** `animateText()` (per-letter / per-word / per-line entrances and exits in one call: `...animateText('Title', style, { x, y, align: 'center', at: 0.5, duration: 5, in: 'rise', out: 'fade', stagger: { each: 0.05 } })`), `splitText()` / `measureText()` (per-letter / per-word layers, exact positions, by hand), `shape: 'arc'` (progress rings, pie / donut slices: animate `endAngle`), `fillGradient` (linear/radial, alpha stops → vignettes), `{value}` counters, `repeat`/`yoyo`, `orbit()`, seeded randomness (`rand(seed)` / `noise(x, seed)` in expressions, `random(seed)` in JS, never `Math.random()`) `wiggle()` (a seeded shake as keyframes; on a camera put it on `offsetX` / `offsetY` so it rides on the move) `cameraPath()` (a camera flight through `[x, y, z]` points as keyframes; layers it passes: `hideBehindCamera: true`) depth of field (camera `focus` + `aperture`: `{ type: 'camera', initial: { focus: 'title' } }` blurs the other threeD layers by depth; a rack focus is a keyframe on `focus`) `music` (a tune with no file: `{ type: 'audio', music: { bpm, tracks: [{ inst: 'keys', notes: 'Cmaj7:4 Am7:4' }, { inst: 'bass', notes: 'c2:2 g1:2' }], drums: { from: 8, kick: 'x...x...' } } }`: notes and chords as text, counted in beats; instruments `keys pluck pad bass sub lead bell musicbox`; `musicEnvelope(music)` feeds `react()`), `audioEnvelope()` / `bpmEnvelope()` + `react()` (visuals that follow music: `const env = await audioEnvelope('music.mp3', { frameRate })` before `movie.init`, then `keyframes: react(env, { duration, props: { scale: { base: 1, amount: 0.4, band: 'bass', release: 0.2 } } })`; `beats: true` pulses on the beats; `bpmEnvelope(120, …)` when there is no file), `deck()` + `Presenter` (a talk as one movie: pages, steps, stops that pause playback, arrow keys / click / swipe to move on: `...deck({ transition: { kind: 'slide', duration: 0.6 }, pages: [{ name, duration, stops, sequences }] })`, `new Presenter(movie, { canvas })` from `pixi-effects/presenter`; G = page overview, P = presenter view with notes and a timer; `pixi-effects-render talk.html -o talk.pdf` = a PDF of the pages), `particles()` (bursts, snow, confetti, sparks as seeded layers: `...particles({ count: 90, at: 2, life: [1, 1.8], area: { x: 640, y: 330 }, speed: [120, 420], gravity: 240, fade: { out: 0.6 } })`), `followPath()` (a layer along an SVG path: `keyframes: followPath({ d, duration, orient: true })`), path morphing (`{ shape: 'path', d, morphTo, initial/keyframes: morph 0 → 1 }`) and `stagger()` (delays for a wave of layers: `stagger(letters, { each: 0.05, from: 'center' })`, or `stagger(n, …)` for numbers; GSAP-style `each` / `amount` / `from` / `grid` / `ease`). **Not in the DSL (hand-roll with a JS loop):** other per-frame curves (waves, spirals: sample them into short linear keyframes). (Draw-on strokes `trimEnd`, text that changes over time `set: { text }` / `visibleChars`, shake `wiggle()` and particles are built in.)
- **Shader layer and warp:** `{ type: 'shader', fragment: 'void mainImage(out vec4 fragColor, in vec2 fragCoord) { … }', uniforms: { speed: 1, tint: '#ff8040' } }` draws a Shadertoy-style formula (GLSL ES 3.00; `iTime` `iResolution` `iFrame` are declared; keyframes move `'uniforms.speed'`; opaque by default; it cannot read the layers behind it; a compile error comes back in your own line numbers). `filters: [{ type: 'warp', kind: 'wave' | 'haze', strength: 6 }]` bends a layer's picture like water or heat.
- **Light, shadow, fog (2.5D):** a `{ type: 'light', kind: 'ambient', initial: { intensity: 0.2 } }` plus a `spot` / `point` / `parallel` light (`castsShadows: true` on the light AND on the `threeD` layers that cast) shades every `threeD` layer by angle and distance; `lit: false` opts a layer out; camera `fogNear` / `fogFar` / `fogColor` fade what is far. What no light reaches is black (add the ambient light); layers are drawn in distance order (no depth buffer). `check --at` prints how lit each layer is.
- **Blend modes:** `blendMode` takes 18 CSS names (`add` `screen` `multiply` `overlay` `soft-light` `hard-light` `color-dodge` `color-burn` `darken` `lighten` `difference` `exclusion` `hue` `saturation` `color` `luminosity` `linear-burn`, hyphenated) on any layer: glows and light leaks (`add`, `color-dodge`), colour casts and contrast (`soft-light`, `overlay`), vignettes (`multiply`). It blends with everything below the layer; on a composition each child blends (as one picture: `threeD: true` or a filter); 10+ of the new modes on screen at once warn; it works with every mask.
- **One `Movie` per page.** A sound effect needs no `duration` (it lasts as long as its clip). Seeking is safe: counters, colours and growing shapes are right after any jump.

## Layout sanity (the cheap bugs a screenshot catches)

Centred text must be positioned by `anchorX/anchorY: 0.5`; estimate text width as ~0.6 × `fontSize` per glyph (monospace) or ~0.8 (heavy sans) and leave margin; captions stay above the bottom 60 px; nothing important within 5 % of the frame edge; a `threeD` layer can be sorted in front of text.

## Files

- For an AI in a chat with no shell, the short version is https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yjmtmtk/pixi-effects/main/ai/CHAT.md (it copies https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yjmtmtk/pixi-effects/main/ai/chat-template.html: one self-contained page that loads from a single CDN and shows warnings in a red box).
- `reference/cheatsheet.md` — every layer type, prop, default and rule on one page.
- `reference/recipes.md` — tested building blocks: slam type, lower-third, marquee, count-up, bar chart, 2.5D title, camera orbit, slideshow with transitions + music, looping, particles, gradients/vignette, three.js metal.
- `reference/pitfalls.md` — the full list of real mistakes, with status.
- `npx pixi-effects check` — the one-command review (see Workflow step 5).
- `template.html` — the starting file. (It loads the released library from a CDN, so it works from any folder.)
- `scripts/save-image.py` — save a `dataURL` result (contact sheet / snapshot) to a PNG.
- Full reference: https://yjmtmtk.github.io/pixi-effects/docs/dsl.md and https://yjmtmtk.github.io/pixi-effects/docs/api.md


<!-- ===== skills/pixi-effects/reference/cheatsheet.md ===== -->

# pixi-effects cheatsheet

A video is **data**: a tree of plain objects. Everything below is a JS object you put in `composition.sequences`. Build repeated structure with JS functions and loops; the spec is just objects.

## Conventions (state once, never guess)

| Thing | Rule |
|---|---|
| Canvas | pixels, origin top-left, `+x` right, `+y` down. Typical: 1280×720 @ 30 fps |
| Angles | **degrees**: `rotation`, `skew*`, `rotationX`, `rotationY` |
| Depth (`z`) | `+z` toward the viewer (bigger, nearer) |
| Numbers | any number may be an **expression string**: `'GW/2 - w/2'`, `'min(W,H)*0.4'` (build-time only; no per-frame time variable). Functions: `min max abs floor ceil round sqrt pow sin cos tan lerp clamp smoothstep mod step`, `PI`, and **seeded** `rand(seed)` (0…1) / `noise(x, seed)` (−1…1): give each layer its own seed, never `Math.random()`. **Relative values** work in a keyframe's `to` / `from` / `set` (not in `initial`, a style, or the start of a `from`+`to`): `'+=36'` / `'-=36'` are measured from where the layer stands, and the right side is an expression (`'-=GW*0.1'`). A slide-in is `from: { x: '-=36' }`, a nudge `to: { y: '+=40' }`; keyframes one after another stack; with `repeat` the same move replays from the same start (it does not stack). Expressions work in layer `x y` and the other numeric props, **not** in `line.from / to`, `polygon.points` or `path.d`: compute those in JS (`const W = 1920`) |
| Colours | `'#rrggbb'` strings or numbers; text colour is `style.fill`, shape colour is `fillColor`/`strokeColor`, image colour is `tint` |
| Z-order | **array order**, later = on top. A layer is hidden (not removed) outside `[at, at+duration)` and keeps its last values |
| Time of a sequence's `at` | seconds from the start of its **parent composition** (default 0) |
| Time of a keyframe's `at` | seconds from the start of **its own layer**; **negative = back from the layer's end** |
| Time of a transition's `at` | seconds from the start of the **parent composition**; negative = back from its end |
| `duration` | defaults to the parent composition's duration |
| Time **inside** a layer | `speed` (a multiplier on the layer: 1 = as is, 2 = twice as fast, 0.5 = slow motion, **negative = backward**) and `time` (seconds of the layer's own content, in `initial` / keyframes: a video's or audio file's position in the file, a composition's local playhead; **negative = back from the end of the content**) on **video, audio file and composition** layers. **The layers inside a composition write `at` / `duration` / `keyframes` in THAT composition's own seconds** (its local time); the composition's own `at`, `duration` and keyframes stay in the outer time. `duration` is always the layer's life in the outer time (`{ duration: 4, speed: 2 }` lives 4 s in the movie and plays 8 s of content; its children, with no `duration` of their own, last those 8 s) |

## Expressions

Operators `+ - * /`, parentheses, unary `-`. Functions `min max abs floor ceil round sqrt pow sin cos tan` (radians; there is **no `pi`**: write `3.14159`).

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `W`, `H` | parent composition size |
| `GW`, `GH` | root (movie) size |
| `w`, `h` | this layer's own size (image/video natural size, text size **after** its style is applied, shape bounds) |
| `cover`, `contain` | scale that makes the layer cover / fit the parent (`scale: 'cover'`) |
| `t`, `d`, `T` | layer start time, layer duration, parent duration |

## Common fields (every layer)

```
name, at, duration,
initial: { ...props applied before any keyframe },
keyframes: [ { at, duration, ease, set | to | from | (from + to), repeat?, yoyo?, repeatDelay? } ],
filters: [ { type: 'chromaKey', keyColor, threshold, smoothing, spill } | { type: 'glow', name?, outerStrength: 3, color: '#ffd166' } /* any named filter, see below */ | { type: 'custom', name, filter: <Pixi Filter> } ],
mask: <a layer spec> | 'matteName' | { layer: 'matteName', channel: 'alpha' | 'luma', invert: true } | [ …refs ], maskInverted,   // an inline mask with no `at` of its own starts and ends with the layer it masks (its keyframes count from that layer's start); an explicit mask `at` is composition time. A NAME points at a sibling layer (the matte, shared by any number of layers, NOT drawn itself, alive for its own `at`/`duration`); a list is an intersection; subtract = `invert: true`
filterArea: { x, y, width, height }   // in the layer's OWN coordinates; lets blur/glow draw past the layer's bounds
threeD: true                          // opt into 2.5D (see below)
blendMode: 'normal' | 'add' | 'screen' | 'multiply' | 'overlay' | 'soft-light' | 'hard-light' | 'color-dodge' | 'color-burn' | 'darken' | 'lighten' | 'difference' | 'exclusion' | 'hue' | 'saturation' | 'color' | 'luminosity' | 'linear-burn'   // CSS names (hyphenated); blends with EVERYTHING BELOW the layer; add / screen brighten (glows), multiply darkens, soft-light / overlay for colour casts and contrast, color-dodge for light sources; on a composition the children each blend (to blend it as one picture: threeD: true or a filter); the 14 new ones cost ~2 ms a layer on WebGL (10+ on screen warns)
```

Animatable props (`initial` / keyframes): `x y alpha rotation scale scaleX scaleY pivotX pivotY anchorX anchorY skewX skewY tint width height visible autoAlpha`, plus for shapes their style/geometry, for text `fill`, for audio `volume`, for 3D `z rotationX rotationY`, filter params as `'filters.<name>.<param>'`, three objects as `'three.<obj>.<path>'`. **These go in `initial` / keyframes, never at the top level of a shape or text layer** (top-level `x`, `rotation`, `strokeColor`, `fillAlpha` each warn "is not a … key"): the top level of a shape holds its geometry (`width height radius d startAngle endAngle cornerRadius anchorX anchorY`), `trimStart` / `trimEnd`, `strokeCap` / `strokeJoin`, `fillGradient`.

Keyframe kinds: `set` (jump at `at`; undone when you seek back), `to` (animate to), `from` (animate from), `from`+`to`; a value may be relative to where the layer stands (`from: { x: '-=36' }` slides in from 36 px to the left of its place). `from` / `from+to` show their start value from the layer's start, so a delayed fade-in needs no `initial.alpha`. `repeat` (finite extra plays), `yoyo`, `repeatDelay` loop any of them (endless repeats are not allowed). `ease` = an ease name (`'none'`, `'power2.out'`, `'expo.out'`, `'back.out(1.7)'`, `'elastic.out(1,0.5)'`, `'sine.inOut'`, `'bounce.out'`, **`'cubic-bezier(.4, 0, .2, 1)'`** (CSS syntax, x1 and x2 in 0…1; `.4, 0, .2, 1` is a gentle in-out; `.2, .8, .2, 1` is FRONT-LOADED, not slow motion: half of the change in the first 13 % of the time, 90 % by 39 %, 99 % by 74 %, then a long settle, so what sits at the END of the content gets the glide; `.2, .8, .5, 1` has a shorter tail). `power1…4` are the powers 2…5: `power2` is a cubic, `power2.in` has done only 12.5 % at half time (42 % at three quarters)… and springs: `'spring(mass, stiffness, damping)'` or `'spring.gentle' | 'snappy' | 'bouncy' | 'wobbly' | 'slow'`; **`duration: 'auto'` = the time the spring takes to settle** (presets, settle time / highest value reached as a multiple of the target: `snappy` 0.42 s / 1.01, `gentle` 0.72 s / 1.02, `bouncy` 1.08 s / 1.28, `slow` 1.29 s / 1.00, `wobbly` 1.61 s / 1.40: time the next beat from these) (real physics; with a number `duration` is the settle time and only the damping ratio shapes it; a damping ratio of 1 or more never overshoots, so `spring(1,170,26)` does not bounce: use damping below 20 at stiffness 170; `'auto'` works on keyframes only, not in `animateText` / `orbit` tweens; a `stagger` ease may be a spring, its delays are held inside the spread). Default ease is linear.

## Layer types

**text** — `text`, `style` (any PixiJS TextStyle field: `fontSize fontFamily fontWeight fill letterSpacing lineHeight align wordWrap wordWrapWidth stroke dropShadow padding`; expressions OK for numbers), `colorSpace`. Default anchor is **top-left**; use `anchorX/anchorY: 0.5` to centre on `x,y`. A text layer has one animatable number, `value`, printed where the text contains `{value}` (`text: '{value} users'`, `initial: { value: 0 }`, keyframe `to: { value: 2480 }`; `format: { decimals, grouping, pad /* zero-pad the whole part: pad 2 → 05 */ }`) — that is how counters work. **Changing text:** a keyframe `set: { text: 'Two' }` swaps the string at that time (undone on seek back; `to` / `from` cannot tween a string); `visibleChars` (number, first N characters; starts at 0 once animated) is a typewriter: `to: { visibleChars: 30 }, duration: 2.4, ease: 'none'` — use `anchorX: 0` + `style.align: 'left'` so it grows rightward. Multi-line text is centre-aligned by default (`style.align: 'left'` to change).

**image** — `asset`, `tint`, `colorSpace: 'rgb'|'oklab'|'oklch'`. Default anchor top-left; natural size = `w`,`h`.

**video** — `asset`, `loop`, `audio`, `volume`, **`speed`**; `initial: { scale: 'cover' }`. `speed: 0.5` slow motion, `speed: -1` backward (it starts at |speed| × `duration`, so a 3 s file with no `duration` plays whole, backward); with no `duration` the layer lasts the file's length ÷ |speed|. For anything that is not one straight speed — a freeze, a ramp, a loop — animate **`time`** (seconds in the file) like any property: `keyframes: [{ at: 0, from: { time: 0 }, to: { time: 2 }, duration: 1 }, { at: 1, to: { time: 2 }, duration: 0.5 }, { at: 1.5, to: { time: 6 }, duration: 3, ease: 'power2.inOut' }]` (play 2 s, hold, then accelerate). `repeat` loops it, `yoyo` ping-pongs. `speed` itself is not animatable (it warns): animate `time`. The sound follows (pitch too, like a tape).

**audio** — a file: `asset`, `loop`, `volume`, `speed` (the pitch follows; `time` keyframes work as for video; not for `sfx` / `music`: change an sfx's `pitch` instead, or put it in a composition and remap that); `volume` (top level, or in `initial` like every other layer's starting values); fade with volume keyframes (`{ at: -2, to: { volume: 0 }, duration: 2 }` fades the last 2 s). Omit `duration` for a one-shot clip: it lasts exactly as long as the clip. With `loop: true` and no `duration` it lasts until the composition ends. An explicit `duration` longer than the clip goes silent after the clip unless `loop: true`.
**Or a sound effect with no file — `sfx`:** `{ type: 'audio', sfx: 'swoosh', at: 2 }` is the whole thing. Presets, default length in s: `click` 0.04 · `pop` 0.12 · `swoosh` 0.5 (loudest 0.16 s in, moves left → right) · `swipe` 0.22 · `hit` 0.7 · `riser` 1 (loudest at its END: `at = hit − duration`) · `chime` 1.4 · `beep` 0.16 · `coin` 0.4 · `glitch` 0.35 · `typewriter` 0.06. Knobs: `sfx: { preset, pitch /* semitones ±24 */, brightness /* −1 dark … 1 bright */, seed /* another take */ }`. **The layer's `duration` IS the sound's length** (omit it; set it to stretch, e.g. a riser; at most 10 s); `volume` is its level (1 = the preset's standard level, peaking at −12 … −18 dBFS by preset; above 1 is allowed: a sparse track of clicks measured −32 LUFS at 0.5 and needed about 2 to reach −24 LUFS). No `loop`: one layer per hit (a JS loop). Custom sound: `sfx: { voices: [{ wave: 'noise' | 'sine' | 'square' | 'saw' | 'triangle', freq: 440 | [from, to], filter: { type: 'lowpass' | 'highpass' | 'bandpass', freq: [from, to] }, envelope: 'fall' | 'bell' | 'swell' | 'hold', pan: [-1, 1] }] }`. The export (mp4 / webm / mov) encodes this same mix (lossy AAC / Opus), on time within a few ms.
**Or music with no file — `music`:** `{ type: 'audio', music: { bpm: 96, tracks: [{ inst: 'keys', notes: 'Cmaj7:4 Am7:4 Dm7:4 G7:4' }, { inst: 'bass', notes: 'c2:2 g1:2 …' }], drums: { kick: 'x...x...', snare: '....x...', hat: 'x.x.x.x.' } } }` — a tune written as text (notes in LOWERCASE `c4:2` in beats, chords start with a CAPITAL `Am7` `G7` `C@4` `Am7/e` (`g7` is a very high note, not G7), `[c4 e4 g4]`, rest `_`, hold `~`, `!` accent; `|` ignored). Instruments `keys pluck pad bass sub lead bell musicbox`; drums `kick snare hat openhat clap rim tom crash shaker sleigh` as 16th-note step strings (`x` hit, `o` soft, `.` none; a list of `{ from, to, … }` for sections). Score options `bpm` (or `[[beat, bpm], …]` for a ritardando) `swing reverb (0–0.6) humanize drumVol grid transpose tail seed`; track options `vol` (or `[[beat, level], …]` for a fade) `pan step strum legato tone reverb attack release ring transpose`. Lasts its notes + tail, ends with the movie, `loop: true` repeats; peaks −6 dBFS at `volume: 1`. `await musicEnvelope(music, { frameRate })` → an envelope for `react()`; `await musicBuffer(music)` → a Web Audio `AudioBuffer` to play yourself.

**shape** — `shape: 'rect' | 'circle' | 'ellipse' | 'arc' | 'line' | 'polygon' | 'path'`:

| shape | geometry (top level **or** in `initial`) |
|---|---|
| rect | `width height cornerRadius anchorX anchorY` |
| circle | `radius anchorX anchorY` |
| ellipse | `radiusX radiusY anchorX anchorY` |
| arc | `radius innerRadius startAngle endAngle` — degrees, **0° = 3 o'clock, clockwise**; centred on `x, y`; stroke only = an open arc line (`strokeCap: 'round'`), with a fill = a sector, with `innerRadius` = a donut slice; a sweep ≥ 360° = a full circle. A progress ring: `startAngle: -90` and animate `endAngle` from −90 to 270 |
| line | `from: [x,y]  to: [x,y]` — plain canvas coordinates (omit `x,y`; if you give them they place the line's midpoint). Stroke in `initial`: `strokeColor`, `strokeWidth` |
| polygon | `points: [[x,y],…]  open` — canvas coordinates like `line` |
| path | `d` (SVG path data) — canvas coordinates like `line`. **Morph:** `morphTo: 'M…Z'` + animate `morph` 0 → 1 (points half way between, closed outlines lined up so they do not twist; `morphPoints` 8–2048) |

**Draw-on:** every shape but `arc` has `trimStart` / `trimEnd` (0–1 of the outline, default 0 / 1, animatable): `trimEnd: 0` + keyframe `to: { trimEnd: 1 }` draws a line / border / path on; `trimStart` 0 → 1 after it wipes it off; both = a travelling dash. The fill is NOT trimmed. Rect outline starts top-left, circle / ellipse at 12 o'clock, both clockwise. A `path` with several sub-paths walks them in order as one length; `trimEach: true` trims each on its own (all draw on together). Use `strokeCap: 'round'`. **Dashes:** there is no dash option; write the outline as alternating sub-paths (`d: 'M 0 0 L 10 0 M 20 0 L 30 0 …'`, or sample the curve) and `trimEnd` 0 → 1 walks them in order, so the dashes draw on one after another (as in `replay-highlight`).

Style (`initial` / keyframes): `fillColor fillAlpha strokeColor strokeAlpha strokeWidth`; `colorSpace: 'oklab'|'oklch'` for clean colour tweens. rect/circle/ellipse are **centred on `x,y` by default** (`anchorX/anchorY` default 0.5): for a bar growing from its base use `anchorY: 1` (or `anchorX: 0` for left-to-right). **`fillGradient`** (top level or `initial`; instead of `fillColor`): `{ type?: 'linear'|'radial', stops: [[0, '#000'], [1, 'rgba(0,0,0,.6)']], angle? /* linear, deg; DEFAULT 90 = top→bottom, 0 = left→right: a wide gradient slid sideways as a matte needs angle: 0 */, center?, innerRadius?, radius? /* radial, 0–1 of the SHAPE's own bounds, not the canvas: a glow on a 1500 px circle is placed with fractions of that circle */ }` — stops may have alpha, so a radial transparent→dark is a vignette. **Animate it** with a partial gradient in a keyframe (`to: { fillGradient: { angle: 360, stops: [...] } }`: keys you leave out stay; the same number of stops; `type` cannot change; a start gradient is required; use `colorSpace: 'oklch'` for a vivid fade). A text layer takes `fillGradient` too (LINEAR only: angle and stops; type / center / radius are ignored with a warning; letters re-rasterised per change). `from` alone runs from that gradient to the layer's own. The names `'fillGradient.angle'` / `gradientAngle` are not properties: write `fillGradient: { angle }`. Stroke ends and corners: `strokeCap: 'butt'|'round'|'square'`, `strokeJoin: 'miter'|'round'|'bevel'` (top level or in `initial`; not animated — `round` keeps sharp corners like an M from poking out).

**composition** — `width height duration sequences transitions`, **`speed`** (the composition's own time: its content plays backward, in slow motion, … — `time` keyframes give a freeze, a rewind, a ramp; a composition's sound and sfx follow; its own x / alpha keyframes stay in the outer time; **children are placed in the composition's local seconds**; the content is as long as the larger of `duration` and the farthest `time` it reaches (`speed: 2` → twice `duration`; `time` keyframes → their largest number), and children default to that length. A child whose life ends exactly where a held `time` stands is hidden during the hold (a life is [at, at + duration)): give it a `duration` that reaches past. `time` keyframes and ordinary ones (`x`, `alpha`, a `wiggle`) may share one `keyframes` list. A sound inside goes silent while the clock stands still). With `threeD: true` it is a **card**: its children are drawn into one texture (content outside its `width × height` is clipped: size it for a soft shadow too; a plain 2D composition does not clip, but is skipped when its whole rectangle is off screen) and move / rotate in depth together. Children use the composition's local coordinates and times. Position/rotate/scale it as a unit; to rotate/scale about its centre set `pivotX/pivotY` to the centre and `x/y` to where that point should sit.

**shader** — `{ type: 'shader', fragment: 'void mainImage(out vec4 fragColor, in vec2 fragCoord) { … }', uniforms: { speed: 1, tint: '#ff8040', pos: [0.5, 0.5] }, width?, height?, resolution?: 0.5, transparent?: false }` — a Shadertoy fragment shader drawn into a layer (GLSL ES 3.00): `iResolution` `iTime` (the layer's own seconds) `iFrame` and your uniforms are declared for you; keyframes move uniforms as `'uniforms.speed'` and components as `'uniforms.tint.0'`; opaque unless `transparent: true`; it cannot read what is behind it (no `iChannel` / `iMouse` / `iDate`); no `while` or non-constant `for`; a compile error is reported in your own line numbers and the layer is a checkerboard.

**null + `parent`** — `{ type: 'null', name: 'rig', initial: { x, y }, keyframes: [...] }` draws nothing; layers with `parent: 'rig'` are drawn inside it and follow its `x y rotation scale skew alpha pivotX pivotY`. Their `x / y` are measured **from the null's origin** (null at (640,360), child `x: 200` → drawn at 840), so rotating the null makes the child circle it. Nulls chain (`parent` on a null). Children are drawn at the null's place in the stack, together. Only `null` layers can be parents; not for `threeD` layers; a mask follows its layer.

**camera** (2.5D) — props in `initial`/keyframes: `x y z lookAtX lookAtY lookAtZ fov focus aperture` (defaults: centred, looking at the z = 0 plane, `fov` 40, `z` auto = `(H/2)/tan(fov/2)` ≈ 989 at 720p). **Depth of field:** `focus` = the sharp plane (a `threeD` layer's name = its first z, or a z number), `aperture` = the lens diameter in px (30 default, 0 off); writing either blurs the other `threeD` layers by their distance from the focus (a rack focus is a keyframe on `focus`; recipe `rack-focus`; `inspect` reports `depthBlur`, and `check --at 2.4` prints each layer's blur). A dolly with no typed distance: leave `z` automatic and animate `offsetZ`. Never on the camera object itself. An orbit is `orbit()`; by hand: `x = cx + R·sin θ`, `z = R·cos θ`, `R = (H/2)/tan(fov/2)`, `lookAt` = the centre at `z = 0`.

**three** (optional entry `pixi-effects/three`) — `three({ type:'three', width, height, setup(ctx) { …; return { objects: { knot } } }, update?, dispose? })`; drive with `'three.knot.rotation.y'` keyframes. Call `registerThree()` before `init`.

## Camera flight and a camera shake

`...cameraPath({ points: [[x, y, z], …], duration, ease, look: 'ahead' | [x, y, z], lookAhead: 0.08, smooth: true, from, to, frameRate })` → camera keyframes (`x y z lookAtX lookAtY lookAtZ`) along a smooth curve at even speed (`ease: 'power2.in'` accelerates). A handheld shake goes on the camera's **offsets** so it never collides with the move: `...wiggle({ duration, props: { offsetX: { around: 0, amp: 5 }, offsetY: {…} } })` (`offsetX/Y/Z`, `lookOffsetX/Y/Z` are added to the position and the look-at point). A threeD layer the camera passes on purpose: `hideBehindCamera: true` (hidden quietly behind the camera, no warning). Recipe `camera-fly-through`.

## 2.5D in one paragraph

Add `threeD: true` to any visual layer, then use `z`, `rotationX`, `rotationY` (centre rotation with `anchorX/Y: 0.5` or `pivotX/Y`). Add a `{ type: 'camera' }` layer for a view. A `threeD` layer at `z: 0` with the default camera looks identical to a 2D one. Consecutive `threeD` layers are drawn farthest-first (equal `z` keeps array order); non-`threeD` layers ignore the camera and keep array order. Layers at/behind the camera plane are hidden. Not supported on `threeD` layers: masks, transitions, `filterArea`. **Light:** `{ type: 'light', kind: 'ambient' | 'point' | 'spot' | 'parallel', falloff?: 'none' | 'smooth' | 'inverseSquare', castsShadows?, initial: { x, y, z, lookAtX, lookAtY, lookAtZ, intensity, color, coneAngle, coneFeather, radius, falloffDistance, shadowDarkness, shadowDiffusion } }` lights every `threeD` layer of the composition (`lit: false` opts out; what no light reaches is black, so add `kind: 'ambient'`); a shadow needs `castsShadows: true` on the light AND on the layer (hard by default, `shadowDiffusion` softens; up to 4 casters per receiver). **Fog:** camera `initial: { fogNear, fogFar, fogColor, fogAmount }` (any one turns it on).

## Poster

`movie.init({ …, poster: 9.5 })` names the moment (seconds; negative = from the end) that stands for the movie: the canvas shows it before play (the playhead stays at 0, play starts from 0), `movie.poster` / `movie.posterFrame` read it, `await movie.posterImage({ as: 'dataURL', type: 'image/jpeg', scale: 0.5 })` is the picture. Pick the most striking moment, not frame 0 (which is often black).

## Player

`new Controller(movie, { canvas, theme: { accent: '#ff4d6d' } })` (import from `pixi-effects/controller`; theme keys `accent foreground track barBackground trackHeight font`, or CSS `--mc-accent` …; `controller.setTheme(…)`). Your own player: `movie.play() pause() gotoFrame(f) volume muted toggleMute()`, state `currentFrame totalFrames frameRate duration isPlaying`, events `ready frame play pause ended seeking seeked volumechange error progress` (`<video>` names). `examples/15-custom-player.html` is a complete one.

## Filters by name (no import)

`filters: [{ type: 'glow', name: 'halo', outerStrength: 3, color: '#ffd166' }]` — `type` = the pixi / pixi-filters class name without `Filter`, camelCase, or this library's own **`warp`** (bends the picture: `{ type: 'warp', kind: 'wave' | 'haze', strength: 6 (px), scale: 80 (px), speed: 0.5, angle: 0, seed: 0 }`; `wave` = a travelling wave, `haze` = drifting noise; moves with the frame's time by itself; options animate by name) or **`grain`** (film grain: `{ type: 'grain', amount: 0.08, size: 1.5, seed: 0, fps: 24, color: 0 }`, seeded, new every 1/fps s, mid-tone weighted, same grain pattern on every GPU (values within 1/255), anchored to the filter's frame (it moves with a layer), no pixi-filters needed; on a layer or on `composition.filters`; it costs video bitrate; `noise` is NOT film grain: it is frozen and lifts blacks) (`glow dropShadow outline blur noise alpha adjustment hslAdjustment grayscale pixelate crt rgbSplit oldFilm glitch bulgePinch twist zoomBlur kawaseBlur radialBlur motionBlur emboss ascii colorOverlay advancedBloom bevel dot crossHatch tiltShift …`), the other keys are its options. `colorMatrix` takes `preset: 'sepia'|'grayscale'|'negative'|'polaroid'|'technicolor'|'vintage'|'kodachrome'|'browni'`. Name it to animate: `'filters.halo.outerStrength'` (scalars only; `pixelate` via `sizeX`/`sizeY`). Options: `glow` distance outerStrength innerStrength color alpha · `dropShadow` offset{x,y} blur alpha color · `outline` thickness color · `blur` strength · `adjustment` gamma contrast saturation brightness · `hslAdjustment` hue lightness saturation · `pixelate` size · `crt` curvature lineWidth noise vignetting · `rgbSplit` red/green/blue {x,y} · `oldFilm` sepia noise scratch vignetting · `glitch` slices offset · `twist` radius angle offset · `bulgePinch` center radius strength · `zoomBlur` strength center innerRadius · `colorOverlay` color alpha · `colorGradient` gradientType('linear'|'radial'|'conic') stops[{offset,color,alpha}] angle · `colorReplace` originalColor targetColor tolerance · `convolution` matrix(9) · `shockwave` / `godray` are driven by `time` (animate it) · `colorMap` / `simpleLightmap` need a texture (use `custom`). **Centres/offsets are CANVAS pixels** (default top-left corner): put them on the layer. Glow / shadow / blur draw outside the layer: widen `filterArea` (not for `grayscale` / `oldFilm`, which fill the margin black). Full table: https://yjmtmtk.github.io/pixi-effects/docs/dsl.md → Named filters.

## Transitions (on the parent composition)

```js
transitions: [{ kind: 'crossfade' | 'wipe' | 'iris' | 'slide' | 'dip' | 'zoom' | 'dissolve' | 'luma',
                from: 'nameA', to: 'nameB', at: 3, duration: 1, ease: 'none',
                direction: 'left|right|up|down' /* wipe, slide */, mode: 'in|out' /* iris, zoom */,
                smoothing, fromScale /* zoom */, scale, seed /* dissolve */,
                map: 'linear' | 'diagonal' | 'radial' | '<grayscale image asset>', softness, flip /* luma */ }]
```
`from`/`to` are sibling layer `name`s, `to` declared after `from`, and both layers must be alive for the whole window (overlap them by `duration`). Only those two layers are affected; every other layer stays put. Wipe/iris/dissolve/zoom wrap the layers for you.

## Presets

```js
import { kenBurns, withFade, wiggle, stagger, followPath, cameraPath, particles, deck, audioEnvelope, bpmEnvelope, musicEnvelope, react, random } from 'pixi-effects';
kenBurns({ asset, name, at, duration, motion: 'still'|'scale'|'rotation'|'position',
           fit: 'cover'|'contain', ease, /* scale */ origin, zoom, direction, /* rotation */ angle, /* position */ from, to })
withFade(spec, { in: 0.5, out: 0.5 })   // alpha fade; `out` needs spec.duration
orbit({ duration: 6, degrees: 40 /* , radius, center, start, fov, ease, at */ })   // a camera layer that circles a point
// a seeded shake as keyframes (spread into a layer's keyframes); each prop moves on its own; ends back at `around`
keyframes: [...wiggle({ duration: 6, freq: 4, seed: 3, props: { x: { around: 'GW/2', amp: 6 }, rotation: { around: 0, amp: 1.5 } } })]
stagger(8, { each: 0.08 /* or amount: total s */, from: 'start'|'end'|'center'|'edges'|'random'|index, grid: [cols, rows], ease, seed })   // → delays [0, 0.08, …]: `at: 1 + d[i]`
stagger(layers, { each: 0.05, from: 'center' })   // → the same layers with `at` pushed back (originals untouched)
keyframes: followPath({ d: 'M 120 560 C 360 120 920 120 1160 560', duration: 4, ease, orient: true /* faces the way it goes; rotate: -90 for an up-pointing image */, from: 0, to: 1, frameRate: 30 /* = the movie's */ })   // x / y (and rotation) along an SVG path; give the layer its own `at`
...particles({ count: 90, at: 2, emit: 0 /* 0 = burst; or seconds to spread births */, life: [1, 1.8], area: { x: 640, y: 330 /*, width, height */ }, angle: [0, 360] /* 0 right, 90 down, −90 up */,
               speed: [120, 420], gravity: 240, wind: 0, drag: 1.2, sway: { amp: 30, freq: 0.6 }, size: [2, 4.5], scale: [1, 0], fade: { in: 0.2, out: 0.6 },
               colors: ['#ffd166', '#ff6b9d'], shape: 'circle'|'rect'|'star', spin: [-200, 200], blendMode: 'add', seed: 1, name: 'burst', template: { type: 'image', asset } })   // seeded layers, paths baked into keyframes
// a presentation: stops pause playback (`composition.stops: [2, { at: 5, page: 'Name', notes, advance, pdf }]`; `pdf: true` = the stop that pictures its page in a PDF, `pdf: false` = keep it out; default the page's last stop; a `page` stop begins a page, the others are steps); deck() lays pages out
await movie.init({ canvas, width, height, frameRate, ...deck({ transition: { kind: 'slide', direction: 'left', duration: 0.6 },
  pages: [{ name: 'Hello', duration: 3.2 /* last stop + transition */, stops: [2.6] /* page-local */, notes, sequences: [ /* page-local time; a step = a layer starting at the previous stop */ ] }] }) });
new Presenter(movie, { canvas });         // import { Presenter } from 'pixi-effects/presenter': → ↓ Space Enter click = next, ← = back, Home / End, number+Enter, B / W, F, ?
movie.next() / prev() / goToStop(i) / goToPage(n) / movie.stops / movie.on('stop', …)   // Controller: marks on the seek bar, play / Space / click = play to the next stop (pauseAtStops: false = straight through), a Present button, PDF in the download panel
// Presenter extras: G = page overview (pictures), P = presenter view (a second window: live picture, next picture, notes, timer); start() makes the pictures before the audience sees anything
await movie.stopImages({ as: 'dataURL', scale: 0.25 }) // [{ stop, page, image }] one per page (its last stop); { which: 'stops' } one per stop (a page's picture honours `pdf` flags)
await movie.inspectStops()                             // { stops, issues }: stops whose picture is still changing (a stop landing before its animation ends); the check lists them
await movie.exportPDF({ title })                       // Blob: a PDF page per page of the deck; CLI: pixi-effects-render talk.html -o talk.pdf (--all-stops)
const env = await audioEnvelope('music.mp3', { frameRate: 30 })   // BEFORE movie.init: .series.level|bass|mid|treble (0–1 per frame), .beats [s], .bpm, .at(t, band); bands: { name: [Hz, Hz] }
const env = bpmEnvelope(120, { duration: 12 })                     // no audio file: kick / snare / hats exactly on a tempo
keyframes: react(env, { duration: 12, props: { scale: { base: 1, amount: 0.4, band: 'bass', attack: 0.02, release: 0.2 }, alpha: { base: 0.4, amount: 0.6, beats: true, decay: 0.15 } }, audioOffset: 0, loop: false })
const r = random(7); r(); r();      // a repeatable stream in 0…1 for JS loops (never Math.random())
```
`kenBurns` covers the canvas, so source images should be at least canvas-sized (1920×1080 for 1280×720).

```js
import { measureText, splitText, animateText } from 'pixi-effects';   // text layout helpers (measured with the renderer's own fonts)
measureText('Hello', style)                              // → { width, height, lines }
splitText('Hello world', style, { by: 'chars' | 'words' | 'lines', x, y, align: 'left' | 'center' | 'right' })
                                                         // → [{ text, x, y, width, index, line }] — one text layer per piece, same style, anchor top-left
```
Per-letter / per-word / per-line animation in one call: `...animateText(text, style, { x, y, align, by: 'chars'|'words'|'lines', at, duration /* required: until the last piece is gone */, in: 'rise'|'drop'|'fade'|'pop'|'zoom'|'slide'|'spin'|{ from, to, duration, ease }|false, out: <same, runs in the same wave BACKWARDS FROM THE LAYER'S END (at + duration): it has no `at`; to be gone at time T set duration = T − at>, stagger: { each, from, … }, idle: { y: 4, rotation: 1 }, styleFor: p => ({ fill }) })` → text layers `<name>-0…` (anchor centre; `x`/`y` in `from` are offsets) to spread into `sequences`. **`x` / `y` are pixel NUMBERS (an expression like `'GW/2'` throws: compute `W / 2`), and `y` is the TOP of the line box**: the visible text is centred `lineHeight / 2` below it, so an underline goes at `y + lineHeight`, not at `y` (recipe `animate-text`). By hand: `splitText(...)` + one layer per piece (recipe `split-text`). A web font must be loaded before measuring.

## Assets

`assets: [{ name, src }]` in `movie.init` (images, audio, video). `src` may be a URL or a `data:`/`blob:` URL (e.g. `canvas.toDataURL()`).

## Movie API

```js
const movie = new Movie();
await movie.init({ canvas, width, height, duration, frameRate, background, assets, composition });
movie.play(); movie.pause();
await movie.gotoFrame(n, true);                 // seek (frames; 30 fps => t = n/30)
const blob = await movie.render({ format: 'mp4' });   // 'mp4' | 'webm' | 'mov' | 'mkv'; ~real-time. `format: 'wav'` / `'ogg'` writes only the movie's SOUND (a `music` score as an audio file). `video: { codec: 'hevc' | 'av1' | 'vp9' | 'avc', bitrate: '8M', hardware, keyFrameInterval }` (a codec this browser cannot encode names the one that works). Part of it: `range: [2, 5]` (seconds) or `range: 'title'` (a top-level layer's span; picture and sound); `scale: 0.5` / `draft: true` (half size, low quality, no motion blur: a smaller file, not a faster drawing). Fast motion: `movie.init({ motionBlur: true })` (8 samples, 180° shutter; or a number / { samples: 2–64, shutter: 0–1 }) blurs render / snapshot / contactSheet, not live playback; a render takes `samples`× as long
movie.on('progress', e => e.progress /* 0–100 */);
movie.audioBuffer                                // mixed audio (after init), if any audio layers
await movie.contactSheet({ count: 6, as: 'dataURL' })   // ONE image of several labelled frames — look at it. Options: frames | times | count, columns, cellWidth, as
await movie.snapshot(60, { as: 'dataURL' })             // one frame, canvas only (no player bar) — use it for detail; sheet tiles are small
await movie.inspect(60, { layers: 'none' })             // issues only (default lists the visible layers); text off-canvas / cut off / empty / overlapping text. Name your layers so paths are readable
await movie.onionSkin({ from: 1, to: 3, count: 8, as: 'dataURL' })  // frames overlaid into ONE picture of a movement (later = stronger): path and easing at a glance
movie.review({ at: 'title@end' })                 // what `pixi-effects-check` looks at, as data: { frames, problems (text cut off, off-canvas, no size), review (text overlaps: look at them), fonts, audio, at }; leaves the movie as it was. `strict: true` makes every issue a problem
movie.resolveAt('3.5, 50%, f120, title@end')      // moments → [{ label, frame }]; a mistake says what could not be read
movie.inspectFonts()                             // { missing: [{ layer, family }] (no font of the list is installed), failed: [web fonts whose file did not load] }
movie.inspectAudio()                             // the soundtrack as numbers; also loudness { integratedLufs, truePeakDb, clippedSamples, silences }, scenes, cues, notes (advice: -14 to -16 LUFS is typical for web video) — — you cannot listen: sources[i] = { layer, start, end, peakDb, sound: { length, peakDb, loudestAt, brightnessHz } } (`peakDb` is the MIX's peak between `start` and `end`, not the layer's own: `sound.peakDb` is the sound's; for a sound inside a remapped composition `start` / `end` span every pass it is heard, forward, backward, replayed, in the movie's seconds), windows (`{ t, rmsDb, peakDb, brightnessHz }` per 0.1 s), issues (limited mix, inaudible / cut-off sounds)
new Controller(movie, { canvas })                // optional player bar (overlays the canvas bottom ~60px; not in the export)
```


<!-- ===== skills/pixi-effects/reference/pitfalls.md ===== -->

# pixi-effects pitfalls — what actually went wrong

Collected by having fresh AI sessions build pieces from the docs alone: first six (kinetic type, news lower-third, slideshow, 2.5D showcase, three.js title, bar chart), then a portfolio of 16 more (items 32 and up), made by three different models. Each entry is a real stumble. **Status**: `fixed` = the library now handles or warns; `docs` = nothing can catch it, so remember it; `hand-roll` = the DSL has no feature, see the workaround.

A good habit that catches most of these: after `init`, read `window.__logs` (see `template.html`) — every pixi-effects warning says what to change.

## Time

1. **Keyframe `at` starts at 0 when THIS layer appears** *(fixed in 0.3.0; earlier versions measured from the composition and failed silently)*. A layer at `at: 2` with a keyframe `at: 0` animates at global 2 s. Negative `at` counts back from the layer's end. A keyframe that starts after its layer ends now warns ("never plays").
2. **A layer's own `at` and a transition's `at` are composition time** (seconds from the parent composition's start). Only keyframes are layer-local.
3. **Layers are hidden, not removed, after `[at, at+duration)`** and keep their last values. Z-order is array order (later = on top). To switch scenes, stack scenes with `at`/`duration`, each starting with an opaque full-screen rect. *(docs)*
4. **Transitions need overlapping lifespans.** Both layers must be alive for the whole window: scene `i` starts at `i·(L−T)`, the transition's `at` is the next scene's start, total = `n·(L−T)+T`. A scene that ends while the transition is still running leaves a gap. *(docs)*
5. **Sound effects need no file at all:** `{ type: 'audio', sfx: 'pop', at }` — the layer lasts exactly as long as the sound. **Audio length of a FILE.** Omit `duration` on a one-shot clip: the layer lasts exactly as long as the file (nothing to measure; the only sample file is `examples/_assets/bgm.mp3`, 6 s). `loop: true` with no `duration` lasts until the composition ends. An explicit `duration` longer than the clip goes silent after the clip unless `loop: true` (`bgm.mp3` is 6 s) and warns. Volume fades work like any keyframe: `volume: 0` + `{ at: 0, to: { volume: v }, duration: 2 }` + `{ at: -2, to: { volume: 0 }, duration: 2 }` (the last 2 s only; `set` is a jump). *(fixed: volume keyframes used to ramp from the previous keyframe's end, so the music faded across the whole piece)*
6. **Snap times to the frame grid (`Math.round(t*30)/30`) when two things must stay locked** (a bar and its label). Drive both from one JS easing function with per-frame `set` keyframes rather than mixing a tween with computed positions. *(docs)*
7. **Pick eases on purpose.** `expo.in` stays tiny until the very end (a "flood" circle never reaches the corners — use a bigger radius and `power2.in`). A zoom transition with `power2.out` looks like a cut because the incoming scene is nearly opaque after 40 %. Default is linear. *(docs)*
8. **`render()` runs in roughly real time** (6 s of 720p ≈ 6 s). Listen to `movie.on('progress', e => e.progress)` (0–100). *(docs)*

## Layout and anchors

9. **Defaults differ by type.** rect/circle/ellipse are centred on `x,y`; text and image are top-left; a composition has no anchor — use `pivotX/pivotY` and set `x,y` to where the pivot should land. For a bar growing from its base use `anchorY: 1` (or `anchorX: 0`). *(docs)*
10. **Shape geometry may be at the top level or in `initial`** (`width height radius anchorX …`). *(fixed: `initial` used to be silently ignored)*
11. **Angles are degrees** — `rotation`, `skew*`, `rotationX/Y` — and `rotation: -0.2` is almost no rotation. *(docs)*
12. **Text**: anchor 0.5 centres the line *box*, not the cap height (an underline under serif or italic text needs ~`0.9·size` below the centre: `0.46·size` touches the descenders of a g or y). Arial Black is ~0.8·size wide per glyph, monospace ~0.6·size; leave ~7 % for hold-scale. `style` accepts any PixiJS TextStyle field: `letterSpacing`, `wordWrap` + `wordWrapWidth`, `lineHeight`, `stroke`, `dropShadow`, `padding`. A glow (`dropShadow` with `blur`) is clipped unless `padding ≥ 2·blur`. *(docs)*
13. **`w` / `h` in expressions** are the layer's own size. For text they now describe the styled text (`x: '-w'` scrolls a marquee fully out). *(fixed)*
14. **Masks live in the parent's coordinate space and do not follow the masked layer.** Reveal by growing the mask's `width` from a fixed edge (`anchorX: 0`); exit by tweening `x` and `width` together; slide the content separately. *(docs)*
15. **`line` / `polygon` / `path` use plain canvas coordinates** when you give no `x,y` (they used to be drawn around (0,0)); with `x,y` those place the shape's centre. Stroke colour and width go in `initial`. A background pill must be sized from its text (~0.58 × fontSize per glyph + padding): `inspect` does not check text against shapes. *(fixed)*
15b. **`filterArea` is in the layer's own coordinates** (origin = its local origin, e.g. a circle's centre), not the parent's. A blurred shape is clipped to its bounding box without it: `filterArea: { x: -(r+260), y: -(r+260), width: 2*(r+260), height: 2*(r+260) }`. `threeD` layers pad automatically. *(docs)*
16. **The player bar overlays the bottom ~60 px of the canvas** in browser screenshots (not in the exported video). `movie.snapshot()` / `movie.contactSheet()` never include it; keep captions above it anyway. *(fixed: use the built-in snapshot tools)*

## Missing features (hand-roll)

17. **Gradients / vignettes**: use shape `fillGradient` (linear or radial, stops may have alpha). Earlier sessions hand-rolled canvas images or dozens of stacked bands. *(fixed)*
18. **Counters**: `text: '{value}'` + animate `value` (with `format`). Other text content cannot change over time. Earlier sessions generated one text layer per number (40+ per bar). *(fixed)*
19. **Loops**: `repeat` (finite) / `yoyo` / `repeatDelay` on any keyframe; infinite repeats are rejected with a warning. *(fixed)*
20. **No per-frame expression time.** Expressions are evaluated once at build. A camera orbit is `orbit()`; a shake or drift is `wiggle()`, travel along a path is `followPath()`, and any other curve (waves, spirals) must be sampled into short linear keyframes (~0.1 s) in a JS loop. **Randomness must be seeded** (`rand(seed)` / `noise(x, seed)` in expressions, `random(seed)` in JS): `Math.random()` makes playback and the exported file disagree. *(partly fixed)*
21. **Per-letter / per-word text is `animateText()` (one call: a layer per piece, a wave in and out) or `splitText()` by hand (one layer per piece, positions measured for you); a group / parent is a `{ type: 'null' }` layer + `parent: 'name'`, no caption-linked-to-slide.** One layer per letter; many layers; seeded random loops (`random(seed)`). *(hand-roll)*
22. **Colour tweens look muddy in RGB** (red→green passes through brown). Use `colorSpace: 'oklab'` or `'oklch'` on the layer. In `oklch`, a nearly grey end (chroma < ~0.08, e.g. `#9a9ab4`) borrows the other end's hue, so grey → yellow no longer flashes through pink. *(docs / fixed)*
23. **Generated images**: `canvas.toDataURL()` as an asset `src` works. Make them ≥ canvas size or `kenBurns` zooms look soft. *(docs)*

## 2.5D / three.js

24. **`threeD` is required** for `z`, `rotationX`, `rotationY` (they warn otherwise). Camera props go in `initial`/keyframes, never on the camera object. `+z` is toward the viewer. *(fixed: warns)*
25. **A layer at/behind the camera plane is hidden** — the default camera sits at `z = (H/2)/tan(fov/2)` ≈ 989 at 720p, fov 40 (≈ 808 at fov 48, lower at higher fov). Keep every layer's `z` below it. *(fixed: warns once)* **It is hidden whole when ANY corner of it passes the camera plane**: a big plane tilted with `rotationX` / `rotationY` (a ground plane, an orbit ring) vanishes as soon as one corner swings behind the camera (the warning then says a corner reaches the plane). Tilt it less, shrink it, or keep the camera clear of its depth range. *(docs / fixed: warns)*
26. **Under a dolly zoom only the `z = 0` plane stays put**; everything nearer balloons and clips. Headline at `z: 0`, near cards `z ≤ ~70`. Perspective also pulls far layers toward the centre: put far cards at the outer x, near cards inward, and keep ~10 % margin for an orbit sweep. `orbit({ dollyZoom: { from, to } })` does both together. *(docs)*
27. **Combining orbit and dolly zoom**: `orbit()` specifies `z`, so it stops following `fov` — write your own `fov` and `z = (H/2)/tan(fov/2)` keyframes for the zoom. *(docs)*
28. **Nearer `threeD` layers sort on top of text** — lay out around them; equal `z` keeps array order. A card (rect + icon + label that move together) is a `composition` with `threeD: true`. A final call-to-action or overlay should be a plain 2D layer (last in the array): it ignores the camera, and fade the 3D scene and headline out before it appears (a dim rect alone leaves them visible). *(docs)*
29. **three.js**: the layer clips at its own rectangle — size it to the area you want and pull the camera back (`z ≈ 5.4` for a radius-1 torus knot at fov 50). Metal needs an environment map (`PMREMGenerator(ctx.renderer)`); `three/addons` is not in the importmap. Route `three` through the importmap so there is one copy. Masks/transitions/`filterArea` are not supported on `threeD` layers. *(docs)*

## Tooling (agent harness)

30. **A scene change must keep the outgoing scene alive until the covering flood / wipe has finished**, and the next scene starts when it is complete; the flood circle must reach the corners (radius ≥ half the diagonal) and use `power2.in`, not `expo.in`. *(docs)*
30b. **Unknown option names now warn** (`contactSheet({ cols: 2 })` → did you mean `columns`; `init({ fps })` → `frameRate`). Layer names show up in `inspect` paths, so give layers a `name`. `inspect` ignores faint (alpha < 0.3) layers and text whose x / y is animated (tickers), so a scrolling marquee is not reported as cut off. Pixi may print `[BindGroup] … destroyed while still bound` warnings at `movie.destroy()`: harmless (playback and seeking never warn). *(docs)*
30c. **Look with the built-in tools, not OS screenshots**: `await movie.contactSheet({ count: 6, as: 'dataURL' })` returns one labelled image of the whole animation; `await movie.inspect(frame)` returns every layer's canvas bounds and `issues`. If you do use a browser tool, `screenshot` needs an **absolute path**, macOS `sed -i` needs `''`, and a static server may redirect `/x.html` → `/x` and drop `?query`. Keep the template's `try/catch` around `init` so failures land in `window.__logs`. Check ≥ 5 timestamps including mid-transition. *(fixed: tools built in)*
31. **Check audio with `movie.inspectAudio()`**: every sound measured on its own (`sound.length`, `peakDb`, `loudestAt`, `brightnessHz`), when it plays, loudness and brightness per 0.1 s window, and `issues` (the mix was limited, a layer is inaudible, an sfx is cut off by the end). Decoding a render by hand is no longer needed: `render()` encodes the same mix, on time in mp4 / mov / webm / mkv. *(fixed)*

31b. **A mistyped `ease` now warns** (`ease: 'power3.outt'` → did you mean `power3.out`). It used to run silently as the default ease (`power1.out`), so the motion changed and nothing said so.
31c. **`draft` and `scale` make the file smaller, not the drawing faster** (measured: a 48 s 1080p film exports in about the same time as a draft; the file is 7× smaller). To save time, export a part (`range` / `--range` / `--scene`), look at single moments (`check --no-export --at …`), and keep motion blur off while you iterate.

## Round 2 — found by building 16 portfolio pieces (examples/gallery)

32. **Seeking is safe now** *(fixed)*: a `set` keyframe (counter value, text fill, image tint, shape style) is undone when you seek back before it, and shapes are redrawn before they are culled, so a rect growing from `width: 0` at the left edge draws after any jump seek (contact sheet, snapshot, scrubbing, export). The old workarounds (`width: 0.01`, a one-frame `to` instead of `set`) are not needed.
33. **A mask starts and ends with the layer it masks** *(fixed)*, so its keyframes count from that layer's start. A mask with an explicit `at` keeps composition time. Before, a mask `at: 0` reveal had finished before a layer that appeared at 8 s, and the layer stayed invisible without any warning.
34. **`from` and `from+to` show their start value from the LAYER's start**, not from the keyframe's `at` (as in GSAP and After Effects): a delayed fade-in `{ at: 2, from: { alpha: 0 }, to: { alpha: 1 } }` needs no `initial.alpha`. To keep the current value until `at` and then jump, use `set`. *(docs)*
35. **One `Movie` per page.** Creating a second Movie (for an isolated repro) and destroying it breaks the first (`null.clear`). Reload instead. *(docs)*
36. **Multi-line text is centre-aligned by default** (`style.align: 'left'` for left-aligned paragraphs). *(docs)*
37. **Composition size.** A 2D composition does not clip its children (a child outside `width × height` still draws), but its rectangle is the culling area: if the whole rectangle is off the canvas the group is skipped even when a child is on screen — keep it near what it draws, or canvas-sized. A `threeD` composition (a card) IS clipped at its `width × height` (it is rendered into a texture that size): size it for the soft shadow too. A growing `threeD` shape or text is fine: its texture is resized in place (it used to warn "destroyed while still bound"). *(measured; docs / fixed)*
38. **Under an orbit the side the camera swings toward becomes the NEAR side**: a "far" card at `z: −200` can be drawn bigger than 1× on that side and run off the frame (`inspect` only checks text). Pull those cards inward / lower `z`, and check a frame at the extreme of the sweep. After `orbit()` ends the default camera returns, so to hold the final pose add a camera layer that starts there. Near particles balloon under a dolly zoom: cap particle `z` at about +150, or one becomes a fake full stop. *(docs)*
39. **`fillGradient` stops span the whole unmasked shape**, not the visible part: under a mask, place the stops for the visible fraction (e.g. 0.64→1). A translucent shape over near-black reads as grey: put the alpha in the gradient stops. *(docs)*
40. **Rotate a polygon / path / line about a chosen point with `pivotX` / `pivotY`** (in the shape's own canvas coordinates; put the same point in `x, y`): `{ points, initial: { pivotX: 600, pivotY: 300, x: 600, y: 300, rotation: 180 } }` turns about the vertex (600, 300) — measured. Without a pivot the shape turns about the centre of its bounds. `anchorX` / `anchorY` do nothing on these shapes (they are for rect / circle / ellipse). *(docs; the gallery wrapped every polygon in a composition unnecessarily)*
41. **Glow a whole set of layers** by putting them in one `composition` with a blur filter and `filterArea` (only a composition carries a filter for its children): wide enough for the blur, and the set is built once, so the extra copy is just a second group. *(docs)*
42. **Transition looks:** the default `dissolve` reads as a hard black-and-white camouflage and `scale: 220` as static; `scale: 90, smoothing: 0.5` is a soft film dissolve. The default edge softness of `iris` (0.02) and `wipe` blurs flat graphics at 720p: `smoothing: 0.004`–`0.01` gives a clean edge. *(docs)*
43. **Layers built in a loop need their z-order planned**: anything pushed to the array after the loop is drawn over what the loop made (rings crossed over a header). Keyframes on different properties of one layer may overlap in time. Keep a subject in the upper ~60 % of a source image if a caption will sit under it (`inspect` does not look at picture content). *(docs)*
44. **Zero-pad a counter with `format: { pad: 2 }`** (`18:42:{value}` shows `18:42:05`). A `{value}` placeholder that nothing sets or animates prints 0 and now warns: `{value}` is reserved, there is no way to print it literally. *(fixed)*
45. **The same mistake in a loop warns once**: the warning "keyframe starts after the layer ends" is summarised after three layers. The usual cause is an off-by-one (`f <= frames` instead of `f < frames`) that puts the last sample exactly at the layer's end. *(fixed)*
46. **Still not in the DSL (hand-roll):** `zIndex` (stack order is list order). *(Earlier round-two notes listed draw-on strokes, changing text, jitter and particle emitters here: they are built in now: `trimEnd`, `set: { text }` / `visibleChars`, `wiggle()`, `particles()`.)*
46b. **Blend modes exist now** (`blendMode`: `add` `screen` `multiply` and, since 0.22, 15 more CSS names (pitfalls 78–80), on any layer, threeD layers and compositions included; a composition's children inherit it). Additive white cores no longer read grey on a coloured background. It also works on a layer with `filters` (a blurred glow with `add` / `multiply`): the mode is applied by the last filter, because a container's blend inside a filter pass multiplied against nothing and rendered black. With `add`, use dim saturated colours: overlaps sum, and near-white sums to pure white. *(fixed)*
47. **Browser tooling: prefer `npx pixi-effects check page.html`** — it runs its own private Chrome, so none of the following can bite. If you drive a browser by hand instead: the `agent-browser` daemon is shared, so a `contactSheet` can come back from another session: after saving an image, look at it and confirm it is YOUR piece. In zsh a variable holding `agent-browser --session x` is not split into words (use a small wrapper script). `inspect` now clips overlaps to the visible area, ignores the two scenes of a running transition, treats text inside a moving (panned) composition as moving, and does not report text scaled to 0 as "no size"; it still does not compare text with picture content or shapes.
48. **A composition's `alpha` is applied to each child separately, not to the flattened group** (measured: two overlapping opaque circles in a composition at `alpha: 0.5` show the lower one through the upper one in the overlap). Fading a group that has overlapping children therefore shows the overlap; fade the children themselves, or keep overlapping parts out of the group. Expressions have no way to read a sibling's size: measure text with `canvas.measureText` (the font string Pixi uses) and compute pill widths in JS. *(docs)*
49. **sfx timing and level.** An sfx layer's `duration` is the sound's length (it stretches, it does not trim). Align the loud point: a `riser` peaks at its end, a `swoosh` 0.16 s in. Many sounds at the same instant add up: above 0.9 the mix is limited and a warning names the layers to turn down. Preset names, knobs and voice fields are closed lists — a guess (`whoosh`, `ding`, `impact`, `sawtooth`, `lp`, `decay`) warns with the right word. *(fixed: warns)*
50. **An image (or video) works as a mask, `maskInverted` included** *(fixed)*: PIXI hides a sprite mask with `renderable = false` and the lifespan toggles used to switch it back on, so the mask picture was drawn over the layer (a white disc) and `maskInverted` looked ignored. Use the picture's alpha (or red channel) as the shape: an opaque word or logo on a transparent canvas image is a text-shaped mask with real glyph edges. A `text` layer also works as a mask (cut to its glyphs; measured with a heavy sans `I`). *(docs / fixed)*
51. **Arcs and rings are `shape: 'arc'`** (`radius`, `innerRadius`, `startAngle`, `endAngle`, degrees; 0° = 3 o'clock, clockwise). A progress ring is an arc with `startAngle: -90` and an animated `endAngle` (−90 → 270); `strokeCap: 'round'` rounds BOTH ends. Fill it for a pie slice, add `innerRadius` for a donut slice (a 120-polygon donut is no longer needed). Style (`strokeColor`, `strokeWidth`, `fillColor`) goes in `initial`; `strokeCap` / `strokeJoin` may be top level. *(fixed)*
52. **Measure and split text with `measureText` / `splitText`, not by hand.** `splitText(text, style, { by, x, y, align })` returns each piece's x / y / width in the renderer's own font metrics (kerning kept; verified: a whole line vs the same line in per-letter layers differs only by anti-aliasing). The pieces are for text layers with the default top-left anchor and the same `style`. Load a web font before measuring (`await document.fonts.load('24px "Name"')`) or the fallback font's widths are used. Size a pill from `measureText(...).width + padding` instead of `0.58 × fontSize × length`. *(fixed)*
53. **Draw-on and typewriter need no masks or per-letter layers.** `trimStart` / `trimEnd` (0–1 of the outline, animatable, every shape but `arc`) draw a stroke on: `trimEnd: 0` plus a keyframe `to: { trimEnd: 1 }`. The fill is not trimmed, so fade `fillAlpha` in afterwards; use `strokeCap: 'round'`. Text changes over time with `set: { text }` (swap at a time) and `visibleChars` (typewriter; left-align it so it grows rightward). A `to: { text }` cannot tween a string and warns. *(fixed)*
54. **A deck page lasts until its last stop plus the transition.** `deck()` lays pages out one after another in page-local time and a `transition` overlaps them: a page shorter than its last stop (or shorter than the transition) loses its final step or flashes. A step is a layer that starts at the previous stop (`at: <previous stop>`), so the thing that appears on a press is fully visible when the movie stops. The transition option is `kind`, not `type`. If the last stop is mid-exit on paper, flag the stop you want in the PDF: `{ at, pdf: true }` (in `deck()`: `stops: [1.2, { at: 3, pdf: true }]`), and `pdf: false` keeps one out.
55. **Presenter and Controller both listen to click and keys.** Use the `Presenter` for a talk (or let the Controller's Present button start one); do not run both on the same canvas yourself. `movie.play()` ignores stops, but the Controller's play button / Space / click-on-picture play to the next stop and pause (`pauseAtStops: false` plays through); `movie.next()` plays to the next stop (a second press skips to it), `prev()` jumps back (nothing plays in reverse).
56. **Analyse audio before `init`, and give it the movie's frame rate.** `const env = await audioEnvelope('music.mp3', { frameRate })` is async; `react()` is pure and bakes the keyframes, so there is no per-frame callback. A custom `bands` list replaces the defaults (include `bass` if you want it; beats are picked there). No file yet: `bpmEnvelope(120, { duration })` is a stand-in with a kick on every beat. Offset the music with `audioOffset` when the audio layer does not start at 0.
57. **Review a deck by its stops, not by its timeline.** `pixi-effects-check` writes `stops.png` (one picture per stop, in order) for a page with `stops`; the picture at a stop is what the audience reads while it waits. A stop that lands a few frames before an animation ends shows it half-finished (also in the PDF): `movie.inspectStops()` / the check's review list names such stops; give an animation a little more time than its step (e.g. the next stop 0.3 s after it ends).
58. **`music` counts BEATS, and every track has to add up.** A token's `:n` is beats (a quarter note), a 4/4 bar is 4: a bar of `c4:1 e4:1 g4:1` is a beat short and every later bar drifts. Keep all tracks the same length (the music lasts the longest; a track of rests `'_:16'` sets a length) and check the printed length with `movie.inspectAudio()`. 6/8 is a bar of 3 beats (dotted quarter `:1.5`, eighth `:0.5`) with `grid: 2`; `grid: 3` is triplet eighths in 4/4.
59. **A groove that must enter late needs `from`, not a long string.** `drums: [{ kick: 'x...' }, { from: 8, snare: '....x...' }]`. Patterns repeat; a drum object is a loop of its longest string. A `crash` on the last bar: its own section `{ from: 28, crash: 'x' }`.
60. **Build-ups are layers and `vol` points, not louder notes.** A track's `vol` can be `[[0, 0], [8, 0.7]]` (a fade over 8 beats); the pad's `attack` can be 2–3 s; enter instruments with rests. Per-note `!` and `,` only accent and soften.
61. **Music is a bed: `volume` 0.5–0.8 under speech or sfx.** At `volume: 1` it peaks at −6 dBFS (an sfx peaks at −12). A layer shorter than the music cuts it with a fade; longer is silent after it unless `loop: true`. Do not also add an mp3 bed.
62. **Chord names are voiced close around octave 3**: use `[c3 g3 e4]` for an exact voicing or `Am7/e` for a bass note; `swing` only moves notes that start on an off-beat eighth (`.5`) or sixteenth (`.75`); the bell and music box ring for `ring` seconds whatever the written length (shorten `ring` for fast bell lines); the synth is a handy bed, not an orchestra: keep tracks to 3–6, vary the bars, and end on the tonic.
63. **`animateText()` / `splitText()`: `x` and `y` are pixel numbers, and `y` is the TOP of the line.** An expression such as `x: 'GW/2'` throws (the letters are measured once, at build time): write `x: W / 2`. The pieces are centred half a line below `y`, so a line drawn under the text goes at `y + lineHeight` (about 1.2 × `fontSize`), not at `y`; look at the contact sheet, the layout check cannot see an underline through a word. (`check` writes into `check-out/` of the current folder unless you pass `--out`.)
64. **`animateText()`: `out` leaves from the END of the layer and has no `at`.** `out: { preset: 'fade', at: 7.6 }` does not make the text leave at 7.6 s: `at` is ignored (now with a warning) and the text stays until `at + duration`. To be gone at time T, set `duration: T − at` (title at 0.4 s that must be gone by 8.0 s: `duration: 7.6`). The same holds for a hand-written exit keyframe: a negative `at` counts back from the end of its own layer, a positive one from the start of its own layer, never from the movie.
65. **A spring that does not spring, and `'auto'` that is not a spring.** `spring(1,170,26)` is critically damped (damping ratio 1): it never overshoots; at stiffness 170 use damping below 20 (`spring(1, 170, 12)`), or pick a preset (`spring.bouncy`, `spring.wobbly`). With a number `duration`, that number is the settle time (mass and stiffness only matter with `duration: 'auto'`). `duration: 'auto'` needs a spring ease (otherwise it warns and uses 0.5 s) and is for keyframes, not for `animateText` / `orbit` tweens. A colour that overshoots is clamped in its colour space; `alpha` past 1 shows nothing.
66. **Animating a gradient: one `fillGradient` object, partial, in the keyframe.** `to: { fillGradient: { angle: 360, stops: [...] } }` (keys you leave out stay). Not `'fillGradient.angle'`, not `gradientAngle`, not `fillGradient: 'red'` (each warns once with what to write). The layer must start with a `fillGradient`; `stops` keep their count; `type` cannot change.
